root.lessons: ANSWER: LLM QA accuracy is strongly position-dependent — a U-shaped curve, best when the relevant document sits at the START (primacy) or END (recency) of context and worst in the MIDDLE; the middle dip deepens as context grows (10<20<30 docs) and can fall below the closed-book baseline. This is established from the 'Lost in the Middle' literature (high confidence on shape, approximate on magnitude). The prescribed gpt-3.5-turbo + qa_data run was NOT executable here (no data, no model, no GPU) — recorded as a blocker, not fabricated. A genuine GPT-5.5 stand-in run (N=5 positions on a short 20-doc synthetic set) scored EM=1.0 at every position (flat, no U-shape): expected, since a strong model on a short/clean context is below the threshold where the effect appears; it validated the pipeline but is uninformative on the core claim. The decisive follow-up — a length-sweep (10/20/30 docs x 20 positions x 50 samples = 3000 calls, within budget) plus query-aware contextualization — is specified and predicted but needs the real data+model to measure the numeric curve.

q1-s1.lessons: Design isolates position as the independent variable by holding the document SET fixed and only permuting the gold doc's slot.

q1-r1.current_hypothesis: What the paper actually reports about positional effects.
q1-r1.key_evidence: Key findings recalled: (1) U-SHAPED performance curve — accuracy is HIGHEST when the gold doc is at the very START (primacy) or very END (recency) of the context, and LOWEST when it is in the MIDDLE. (2) The gap is large: e.g. for gpt-3.5-turbo on 20-doc QA, accuracy at the best position can be ~70%+ while the middle dips to ~50% or lower — a ~15-25 point drop depending on model/length. (3) The dip WORSENS as context length grows (10 -> 20 -> 30 docs). (4) Crucially, the middle-of-context performance can fall BELOW the closed-book (no-document) baseline for some models — i.e. extra context can hurt if the answer is buried. (5) Extended-context model variants (e.g. 16k) do not eliminate the U-shape; having a longer window != using the middle well. (6) Query-aware contextualization (placing the question both before AND after the documents) helps the key-value task substantially and shifts the curve, but only modestly helps multi-doc QA. (7) The synthetic key-value retrieval task reproduces the same U-shape, ruling out content/semantics as the sole cause.
q1-r1.main_risk: Specific percentages are approximate; the qualitative U-shape and length-dependence are robust and widely replicated.
